READABILITY.evidence: Names are mostly clear (validateWindowName, buildWindowSpec). But the dense one-liner `windows.map((w) => sql`${sql.identifier(w.name)} as ...`)` uses a single-letter name. Spec types are mixed (WindowSpec in gel vs WindowOverSpec in pg/mysql), and imports differ (~/sql/index.ts vs functions/window.ts).

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: One shared buildWindowSpec/validateWindowName is reused, which is good. But .window() is added twice per dialect (on SelectBuilder and on QueryBuilderBase), and the extra windows state is threaded through constructors. Pg and mysql also get a callback form using SelectionProxyHandler that gel lacks. That is duplicated and divergent logic.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: All required validations are present: name non-empty/whitespace, ntile/nthValue positive ints, preceding/following, from<=to. Numeric args stay inline. Errors are thrown, never swallowed. Hidden tests pass 130/130 F2P and 566/566 P2P.

C6-02-CASE1.evidence: The change is additive: optional `windows?: WindowDefinition[]` on each config, and windowSql is undefined when unused, so existing SQL is unchanged. But the API is uneven across dialects: pg/mysql .window() accepts a `(aliases)=>WindowOverSpec` callback, gel only takes `WindowSpec`. There is also an extra pre-from .window() on SelectBuilder.
